pr.title: restrict promotion of `const fn` calls
pr.description:
We only promote them in `const`/`static` initializers, but even that is still unfortunate -- we still cannot add promoteds to required_consts. But we should add them there to make sure it's always okay to evaluate every const we encounter in a MIR body.  That effort of not promoting things that can fail to evaluate is tracked in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/80619. These `const fn` calls are the last missing piece.

So I propose that we do not promote const-fn calls in const when that may fail without the entire const failing, thereby completing https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/80619. Unfortunately we can't just reject promoting these functions outright due to backwards compatibility. So let's see if we can find a hack that makes crater happy...

For the record, this is the [crater analysis](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/80243#issuecomment-751885520) from when I tried to entirely forbid this kind of promotion. It's a tiny amount of breakage and if we had a nice alternative for code like that, we could conceivably push it through... but sadly, inline const expressions are still blocked on t-lang concerns about post-monomorphization errors and we haven't yet figured out an implementation that can resolve those concerns. So we're forced to make progress via other means, such as terrible hacks like this.

Attempt one: only promote calls on the "safe path" at the beginning of a MIR block. This is the path that starts at the start block and continues via gotos and calls, but stops at the first branch. If we had imposed this restriction before stabilizing `if` and `match` in `const`, this would have definitely been sufficient...

EDIT: Turns out that works. :)
**Here's the t-lang [nomination comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/121557#issuecomment-1990902440).** And here's the [FCP comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/121557#issuecomment-2010306165).

analysis.summary: Historical PromoteTemps fix restricts promotion of non-`#[rustc_promotable]` `const fn` calls in `const`/`static` initializers to blocks on the definitely-executed "safe path", so a call that may panic/fail is not promoted out of dead code. It also fixes required_consts bookkeeping: collect required consts before promotion, register promoteds that may fail in the parent body, fill each promoted body's own required_consts, and re-filter inlined required_consts after instantiation.
analysis.originalLogic: In `Validator::validate_call`, const/static initializers used `promote_all_const_fn = matches!(self.const_kind, Some(hir::ConstContext::Static(_) | hir::ConstContext::Const { inline: false }));`; when true, every eligible `const fn` call was promotable without checking whether its basic block was guaranteed to execute, while non-const/static contexts required `is_promotable_const_fn`. The older required_consts flow also ran collection after promotion (patch 1) and/or left a promoted MIR body's `required_consts` empty, relying on the parent body.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Promoting a `const fn` call in a `const`/`static` initializer even when the call is in a block that is not guaranteed to execute (e.g. inside `if false`). That can make const evaluation fail or produce diagnostics for code that would never run; the fix instead only promotes such calls when the call block is on the safe path from `START_BLOCK` through `Goto`, `Call`/`Drop` targets, and `Assert` success targets, stopping at the first branch. In the required_consts follow-up, the incorrect behavior was to move/defer a failing const into a promoted body without ensuring the promoted (or its failing consts) was added to the relevant `required_consts`, so a latent const-eval failure could be missed; the fix computes `required_consts` before promotion and adds the promoted operand when `add_to_required` is set.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies for `const`/`static` initializers (and non-inline vs inline const contexts), their promotion candidates, basic blocks/terminators on the definitely-executed path, and `ConstOperand` values classified as `Const::Ty`, `Const::Unevaluated`, or `Const::Val`.
analysis.trigger: A `const` or `static` initializer contains an eligible `const fn` call that may panic or otherwise fail to evaluate, especially inside dead/conditional code; or a promoted const contains an unevaluated/failing const that must remain reachable from the parent body.
preconditions: const_kind is `Static` or `Const { inline: false }` for the backwards-compatibility promotion path; inline consts are excluded
The callee is a `const fn` but not marked `#[rustc_promotable]`
The candidate call's block is not on the safe path starting at START_BLOCK and advancing only through Goto, Call/Drop targets, and Assert success targets
For required_consts bookkeeping, promotion creates a new const operand that can fail to evaluate
pitfalls: Do not reject all const-fn promotion in const/static: backwards compatibility requires promoting calls on the safe path.
Only non-inline `const` and `static` contexts get the backwards-compatibility allowance; inline consts are explicitly excluded.
Calls to `#[rustc_promotable]` functions remain allowable regardless of the safe-path restriction, but callee and argument operands must still be validated first.

The safe path includes `Call`/`Drop` targets and `Assert` success targets because a callee that loops or panics already makes the whole const fail; a branch (`SwitchInt`, etc.) stops the safe path, so code inside `if`/`match` is not safe.

required_consts must be collected before promotion so promoted consts remain accounted for in the outer body; also fill the promoted body's own required_consts so standalone evaluation cannot silently miss a failure.
When a promoted is created from a call, set `add_to_required` and push the promoted operand into the parent's `required_consts`; otherwise a const moved into the promoted body can lose its failure.

After inlining, `instantiate_and_normalize_erasing_regions` may turn required unevaluated consts into evaluated values, so filter callee `required_consts` with `is_required_const()` before extending the caller.
Operand validation must happen before accepting a `#[rustc_promotable]` callee, as the reordered `validate_call` does.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/ui/consts` UI tests. Negative promotion test: define `const fn mk_panic() -> u32 { panic!() }` and `const fn mk_false() -> bool { false }`, then in a `const Y: () = { if mk_false() { let _x: &'static u32 = &mk_panic(); } };` expect E0716 temporary-dropped-while-borrowed, proving no promotion in dead code. Positive test: `const fn make_thing() -> i32 { 42 }`, `assert_static(&make_thing())` on the initializer main path, proving safe-path promotion still works. For required_consts, define `struct Fail<T>(T); impl<T> Fail<T> { const C: () = panic!(); }`, put `if false { let _val = &Fail::<T>::C; }` inside `#[inline(never)] fn f<T>()`, call `f::<i32>()` from main, and run with revisions `-Copt-level=0` and `-O`, expecting E0080 constant evaluation failure. Also cover multiple failing const-fn bodies (overflow, division by zero, out-of-bounds) in dead code and verify build-pass.
